free_tier.stated: Unlimited cloud storage for GoPro content, meaning footage captured with a GoPro camera excluding Fusion, on any paid tier, plus 100 GB for non-GoPro content on Premium at USD 59.99/yr or 500 GB on Premium+ at USD 99.99/yr
free_tier.notes: unlimited applies to provenance, not to bytes: the terms draw the line at content captured with a GoPro camera

per_object_cap.stated: Not published as a byte cap. Non-GoPro storage is restricted to MP4, Quicktime/MOV, JPEG, ASF and PNG files

retention.stated: While the subscription is active. No retention clock published

egress.terms: CDN downloads of originals with no published cap; access is by a bearer token against api.gopro.com

tooling: reverse-engineered and read-only in every public wrapper: himewel/gopro-api in Python, dustin/gopro in Go with 139 stars and a push on 2026-10-13, gsora/gpdwn, mvisonneau/gpcd. All of them search, download and sync; none uploads. Auth is a bearer token lifted from a plus.gopro.com web session
chaining: The most valuable unresolved lead in its group and it is one upload experiment, not a research question. The terms draw the line at provenance by device, not by file inspection, so if ingest does not verify capture provenance then unlimited capacity at USD 59.99/yr exists; if it does, the offer collapses to 100 or 500 GB

limits.value: unlimited applies only to content captured with a GoPro camera, plus media trimmed from it in the Quik app; GoPro footage edited with non-GoPro software and re-imported counts as non-GoPro
non-GoPro storage is limited to MP4, Quicktime/MOV, JPEG, ASF and PNG files

identity_cost.detail: a credit card or other payment method at sign-up, including for the Free Introductory Trial

reliability_note: No public wrapper implements upload, so the write path is undocumented rather than absent: the Quik app clearly uploads. Treat the write path as unproven. The supported non-GoPro file types are MP4, Quicktime/MOV, JPEG, ASF and PNG

evidence.proved: 'You receive unlimited cloud storage for content You capture with a GoPro camera (excluding Fusion)'; 'up to 100GB of cloud storage for content You capture with a non-GoPro camera'; 'Storage of non-GoPro footage is limited to the file types listed'
Premium USD 59.99/yr with unlimited GoPro and 100 GB non-GoPro; Premium+ USD 99.99/yr with 500 GB
'Unofficial Python client for the GoPro cloud / Quik HTTP API at api.gopro.com: search your library and fetch download metadata', download only
139 stars, last push 2026-10-13, sync and download with no upload
GoPro's own forum, users asking for upload functionality, which confirms there is no official upload API
the article now renders and lists the non-GoPro types: MP4, Quicktime/MOV, JPEG, ASF, PNG

evidence.proved: media trimmed from GoPro-captured content in Quik counts as GoPro content (unlimited); the same article lists GoPro footage edited in non-GoPro software as non-GoPro content
evidence.quote: Any new, trimmed media made from content captured with a GoPro camera and trimmed using the Quik app (mobile or desktop) and uploaded to GoPro Cloud.

evidence.proved: sign-up requires a credit card or other payment method, for the free introductory trial too
evidence.quote: You must provide a credit card or other payment method at sign-up to ensure uninterrupted access to the Subscription at the end of the Free Introductory Trial

evidence.proved: Premium is still USD 59.99/yr with unlimited GoPro content and 100 GB non-GoPro
evidence.quote: | GoPro Premium12 | Unlimited GoPro plus 100 GB non-GoPro Footage: $59.99/yr |

evidence.proved: Premium+ is USD 99.99/yr with 500 GB non-GoPro
evidence.quote: | GoPro Premium+13 | Unlimited GoPro plus 500 GB non-GoPro Footage: $99.99/yr |

evidence.proved: the terms, effective 2026-04-17, still give unlimited storage for content captured with a GoPro camera excluding Fusion
evidence.quote: You receive unlimited cloud storage for content You capture with a GoPro camera (excluding Fusion), subject to the compatibility limitations listed

evidence.proved: non-GoPro content, and GoPro footage edited or imported by third-party software, is allocated 100 GB
evidence.quote: You are allocated up to 100GB of cloud storage for content You capture with a non-GoPro camera or device and content captured by a GoPro camera that is subsequently edited by (or imported from) a third party software application.

evidence.proved: uploads of non-GoPro content past the limit may be restricted
evidence.quote: Once You reach Your cloud storage limit for non-GoPro footage, GoPro may restrict the upload of any additional non-GoPro content to the GoPro cloud.

price_per_tb_month: USD 59.99/yr Premium and USD 99.99/yr Premium+, which is about USD 120/TB/yr on the 500 GB non-GoPro half and approaches zero on the GoPro half
binding_note: The capacity is unlimited on paper and the gate is a provenance rule plus an upload path nobody has documented. Until one large non-GoPro file is uploaded and accepted, the offer is 100 GB at USD 59.99/yr, which is bad.
notes: The price on the non-GoPro half is about USD 120/TB/yr, so the whole value is in whether provenance is checked.

extras.upload_api: none documented; the Quik app uploads but no wrapper implements it
extras.test_that_settles_it: one account, one large non-GoPro upload, then read the quota back through api.gopro.com
